subject: general
question: In 1892, the Indian National Congress passed a significant resolution at its Allahabad Session, which was a demand for the inclusion of Indians in which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Legislative Council**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1892, during the Allahabad Session of the Indian National Congress, a resolution was passed demanding **increased representation of Indians in the Legislative Council**.
 
• The resolution was part of the early phase of the Congress, which focused on **constitutional reforms and political representation**.
 
• The demands aimed at ensuring that Indians had a voice in the governance of the country under British rule.
 
• This resolution marked a significant step in the gradual evolution of the Indian National Congress's political objectives.
 
• Such demands eventually laid the groundwork for **subsequent reforms like the Indian Councils Act of 1892**, which allowed limited Indian participation in the legislative process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Councils Act of 1892**

 
 
• The Indian Councils Act of 1892 was an important legislative reform introduced by the British government.
 
• It expanded the powers of Legislative Councils, allowing members to **ask questions on the budget and other public matters**.
 
• While the Act was limited in scope, it was a small step toward involving Indians in governance.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**
 
 
• The INC was founded in 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Dinshaw Wacha.
 
• In its early years, the Congress focused on **moderate demands**, such as representation in councils and administrative reforms.
 
 
 
• **Allahabad Session of 1892**
 
 
• This session reflected the growing **demand for political rights** among Indians.
 
• It highlighted the role of the Congress in articulating constitutional demands during the pre-Gandhian era.
 
 
 
• **Viceroy’s Legislative Council**
 
 
• Under British rule, the Viceroy's Legislative Council was the primary legislative body.
 
• Indians were initially excluded but were gradually allowed limited participation following persistent demands.
